newsitem.title: USA: DeVry trims stock offer to 1.8 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: DeVry trims stock offer to 1.8 mln shares.

text.p: DeVry Inc said Thursday it has filed a revised registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission reducing the size of its planned offering of common stock to 1.8 million from 2.0 million shares.
Shares offered by the company will be increased to 1.2 million from 1.0 million and shares offered by officers and directors will be reduced to 600,000 from 1.0 million shares.
DeVry Chairman Dennis Keller has withdrawn the 200,000 shares he had proposed to offer, the company said.
The over-allotment option (which has been reduced to 270,000 from 300,000 shares), if any, will be provided by a selling stockholder.

DeVry said it intends to use substantially all of the net proceeds to repay debt, which has been incurred in connection with the acquisition of Becker CPA Review, and for general corporate purposes. The company may use also use the funds for capital expenditures, for the purchase of properties for new DeVry Institutes and for possible future acquisitions of complementary businesses.
DeVry said it currently has no agreements, commitments or understandings with respect to any acquisitions.
Underwriters are led by Smith Barney Inc, ABN AMRO Chicago Corp, Alex. Brown & Sons Inc and Credit Suisse First Boston Corp.
DeVry operates educational institutions including DeVry Institutes, Keller Graduate School of Management, Becker CPA Review and Corporate Educational Services.
